components.name: DHT11 Temperature & Humidity
components.description: Low-cost digital temperature and humidity sensor with a single-wire interface.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness answers the MCU's one-wire start signal with the DHT11 bit train at datasheet timings (80 us low + 80 us high, then 40 bits of 50 us low with a 27 us or 70 us high), so a hand-written or library reader that times the line with micros() works. DATA is resolved from `pin_map` (the same firmware-pin -> component-id map as the HC-SR04). DHT11 integer encoding: humidity, 0, temperature, 0, checksum. Values come from `temp_c`/`humidity`. Not modelled: the <0.5 Hz sample rate and hold-off, power-on settling, timing jitter, and the pull-up resistor value (the line is ideal).

components.name: DHT22 / AM2302 Temperature & Humidity
components.description: Higher-accuracy digital temperature and humidity sensor.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness answers the MCU's one-wire start signal with the DHT22 bit train at datasheet timings (80 us low + 80 us high, then 40 bits of 50 us low with a 27 us or 70 us high), so a hand-written or library reader that times the line with micros() works. DATA is resolved from `pin_map`. DHT22 encoding: 16-bit humidity (tenths of %), 16-bit temperature (tenths of degC, bit 15 = sign), checksum; values come from `temp_c`/`humidity`. Not modelled: the <0.5 Hz sample rate and hold-off, power-on settling, timing jitter, and the pull-up resistor value.

components.name: SHT31 Temperature & Humidity
components.description: High-accuracy I2C temperature and humidity sensor.

corrupt_crc.label: Corrupt the CRC (tests a driver's validation)

components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves the sensor's I2C interface, so a hand-written or library driver reads real data. It accepts the part's 16-bit commands (0x2400/0x2406/0x240B measure, 0xF32D soft reset, 0x306D/0xE000 heater) and answers a read with six bytes - temperature MSB/LSB + CRC-8, humidity MSB/LSB + CRC-8 - using the SHT3x checksum (poly 0x31, init 0xFF; it matches the datasheet's 0xBE 0xEF -> 0x92 vector). Values come from `temp_c`/`humidity` (T = -45 + 175*raw/65535, RH = 100*raw/65535). Set `corrupt_crc` to break the temperature checksum and exercise a driver's error path. Not modelled: the ~15 ms measurement latency (data is available immediately, so any driver that waits or polls works), clock stretching, the internal heater's thermal effect, and I2C bus capacitance.

components.name: BME280 Environment Sensor
components.description: Temperature, humidity and barometric pressure sensor (I2C / SPI).
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves a BME280 register file on the I2C bus while firmware runs (attach_devices). Chip ID at 0xD0 and raw data at 0xF7..0xFE (pressure, temperature, humidity for the BME280), with a pointer + auto-increment shape. Calibration coefficients are zeroed, so a driver applying the datasheet compensation computes a consistent but uncalibrated value. The 1-Wire/pressure/humidity values come from temp_c/humidity/pressure params.

components.name: DS18B20 Digital Temperature
components.description: Waterproof digital temperature sensor on a 1-Wire bus.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves the 1-Wire bus itself, so a hand-written or library driver works through real bit slots - a reset (any low of >= 480 us) is answered with a presence pulse, the master's slots are decoded by their low time (60-120 us is a 0, 1-15 us is a 1) and the part drives the line itself to serve bytes. Protocol: READ ROM (0x33: family 0x28 + a fixed serial + CRC-8), MATCH ROM (0x55 - a ROM that is not the part's makes it stay silent for the rest of the transaction), SKIP ROM (0xCC), CONVERT T (0x44), READ/WRITE SCRATCHPAD (0xBE/0x4E), COPY/RECALL E2 (0x48/0xB8). The scratchpad is [temp LSB, temp MSB, TH, TL, config, 0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF, CRC-8] with the temperature a 12-bit two's-complement count of 0.0625 degC taken from `temp_c`, and the config byte's resolution bits quantise it (a 10-bit read of 23.1 C reports 23.0 C). DQ is resolved from `pin_map`, and the harness models the bus pull-up (the real module needs a 4.7k resistor). Not modelled: SEARCH ROM / ALARM SEARCH, the alarm function and the TH/TL compares, parasite power, conversion timing (the payload is complete as soon as 0x44 is decoded, so waiting 750 ms or polling both work), the EEPROM behind COPY/RECALL (nothing persists between runs), and the pull-up resistor's value.

components.name: LM35 Analog Temperature
components.description: Analog temperature sensor, 10 mV/degC, TO-92. Pins: +VS, VOUT, GND.
components.notes: Ideal linear output VOUT = 10 mV/degC * T; the temperature is a stimulus you set. Supply, accuracy and self-heating are not simulated.

components.name: TMP36 Analog Temperature

components.name: LDR Light Sensor Module

components.name: Soil Moisture Sensor

components.notes: Only the digital output (DO) is modelled (an ideal push-pull level set by the 'detected' stimulus; AO, supply and thresholds are not simulated). Resistive probes corrode over time; capacitive probes are preferred for long-term use.

components.name: HC-SR04 Ultrasonic Distance
components.description: Ultrasonic distance sensor with separate trigger and echo pins.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model. The harness watches the firmware's TRIG pulse and drives the ECHO pin (an MCU input) high for a distance-proportional time (58 us per cm round trip, 200 us propagation delay), so pulseIn() measures a real echo. Wire TRIG/ECHO to `mcu_pin` components and map them with run_firmware(pin_map, ...). Echo output is 5 V; level-shift when driving a 3.3 V MCU input. Timing is an idealisation: no acoustic spread, min/max range, temperature or 60 ms cycle limit.

components.name: VL53L0X Time-of-Flight Distance
components.description: Laser time-of-flight distance sensor, I2C.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves a VL53L0X register file on the I2C bus while firmware runs (attach_devices). Chip ID (0xEE) at 0xC0 and the measured distance in millimetres at 0x1A..0x1B (16-bit, MSB first), with a pointer + auto-increment shape. Calibration, ranging modes and the interrupt/GPIO behaviour are not modelled.

components.name: HC-SR501 PIR Motion Sensor
components.description: Passive-infrared motion detector with a digital output.
components.notes: The digital output (OUT/DO) is an ideal push-pull logic level set by the 'detected' stimulus. Supply, thresholds/timing and any analog output (AO) are not simulated.

components.name: IR Obstacle Sensor
components.description: Infrared reflective obstacle/proximity sensor module.
components.notes: The digital output (OUT/DO) is an ideal push-pull logic level set by the 'detected' stimulus. Supply, thresholds/timing and any analog output (AO) are not simulated.

components.name: Hall-Effect Sensor (A3144)
components.description: Digital unipolar Hall-effect switch.
components.notes: The digital output (OUT/DO) is an ideal push-pull logic level set by the 'detected' stimulus. Supply, thresholds/timing and any analog output (AO) are not simulated.

components.name: Rotary Encoder (with switch)
components.description: Incremental rotary encoder with quadrature outputs and a push switch.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness drives the A/B quadrature pair through a one-bit-at-a-time Gray cycle, so a polling decoder on the MCU sees every step, and reports the emitted steps under run_firmware's pin_devices. A/B are resolved from `pin_map` (the same firmware-pin -> component-id map as the HC-SR04). Not modelled: contact bounce/detents (steps are ideal), acceleration, the push switch (SW is a plain digital input you can wire to an mcu_pin), and any electrical loading.

components.name: Limit Switch
components.description: Mechanical end-stop switch. COM, NO and NC contacts.
components.notes: SPDT contact: COM-NO closes and COM-NC opens when actuated. Contact bounce is not simulated.

components.name: MPU-6050 IMU
components.description: 6-axis accelerometer and gyroscope, I2C.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves an MPU-6050 register file on the I2C bus while firmware runs (attach_devices). A write transaction's first byte sets the register pointer and further bytes auto-increment; reads return and auto-increment, so a burst read of 0x3B..0x48 works. WHO_AM_I (0x75) is 0x68 and the sample accel/temp/gyro registers are filled from the `ax`..`gz` and `temp_c` parameters (full-scale defaults: 16384 LSB/g, 131 LSB/(deg/s), 340 LSB/degC). Configuration registers (DMP, FIFO, filters, interrupts, INT pin) and timing/self-test are not modelled.

components.name: ADXL345 Accelerometer
components.description: 3-axis digital accelerometer (I2C / SPI).
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves an ADXL345 register file on the I2C bus while firmware runs (attach_devices), with the same pointer + auto-increment shape as the MPU-6050 but the ADXL345's own map. DEVID (0x00) is 0xE5 and the sample g values come from the `ax`/`ay`/`az` parameters, scaled by the scale the firmware itself selected: DATA_FORMAT (0x31) FULL_RES (bit 3) gives 3.9 mg/LSB (256 LSB/g) at every range, and in 10-bit mode it is 256 >> range LSB/g (so +/-4 g is 128 LSB/g). The DATA registers (0x32..0x37) are little-endian 16-bit two's complement and are computed from the live configuration, so a sketch that changes the range sees the counts change. Not modelled: the SPI interface (this part is I2C here), FIFO, tap/double-tap/free-fall/activity interrupts and the INT1/INT2 pins, self-test, offset registers, the 2 g/4 g/8 g output data rate and bandwidth corners, and the part's electrical loading.

components.name: HX711 Load-Cell Amplifier
components.description: 24-bit load-cell amplifier with a simple two-wire interface.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves the HX711 on two MCU pins (DT data-ready/output, SCK clock input). DT goes low when data is ready and the 24-bit value is clocked out MSB-first by SCK pulses; 25/26/27 pulses set gain (128/32/64). DT and SCK are resolved from pin_map. The analog front end (load cell, gain, noise) is not modelled; value comes from the value param.

components.name: Load Cell 5 kg
components.description: Bar-type strain-gauge load cell with a four-wire bridge (E+, E-, A+, A-).
components.notes: Wheatstone bridge of four strain gauges; arm resistance shifts linearly with load. The A+/A- output is a few mV and needs an amplifier (e.g. HX711).

components.name: MQ-2 Combustible Gas Sensor
components.description: Analog gas sensor for LPG, methane, propane and smoke. Needs warm-up.
components.notes: Only the digital output (DO) is modelled (an ideal push-pull level set by the 'detected' stimulus; AO, supply and thresholds are not simulated). Requires burn-in and calibration; cross-sensitive to multiple gases.

components.name: MQ-135 Air Quality Sensor
components.description: Analog air-quality sensor for NH3, benzene, smoke and CO2-equivalent readings.
components.notes: Only the digital output (DO) is modelled (an ideal push-pull level set by the 'detected' stimulus; AO, supply and thresholds are not simulated). Provides an estimated air-quality signal, not a calibrated CO2 measurement.

components.name: CCS811 eCO2 / TVOC Sensor
components.description: Metal-oxide sensor giving eCO2 and TVOC estimates over I2C.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves a CCS811 register file on the I2C bus while firmware runs (attach_devices). Chip ID (0x81) at 0x20, status at 0x00, eCO2 (ppm) at 0x02..0x03 and TVOC (ppb) at 0x04..0x05, with a pointer + auto-increment shape. Baseline/compensation, the WAKE pin electrical behaviour, and the 48 h burn-in are not modelled.

components.name: SCD40 true CO2 Sensor (NDIR)
components.description: Photoacoustic true CO2 sensor with humidity and temperature, I2C.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves an SCD40 on the I2C bus while firmware runs (attach_devices). Command 0x21B1 triggers a single-shot measurement; a read returns 9 bytes (CO2, temperature, humidity, each with a CRC-8, poly 0x31 init 0xFF). Values come from co2/temp_c/humidity. The 5 s measurement cycle, ASC, and the FRC are not modelled.

components.name: PMS5003 Particulate Matter Sensor
components.description: Laser particle counter reporting PM1.0 / PM2.5 / PM10 over UART.

components.name: pH Sensor Module
components.description: Analog pH interface board for water and soil solutions; requires calibration.
components.notes: Probes require regular two-point calibration; results are not temperature-compensated by default.

components.name: EC / TDS Sensor Module
components.description: Analog electrical-conductivity / TDS interface for nutrient and water monitoring.

components.name: PT100 RTD
components.description: Platinum resistance temperature detector (100 ohm at 0 degC).
components.notes: Linear RTD model R = R0*(1 + 0.00385*T). 2/3/4-wire wiring and self-heating are not simulated.

components.name: MAX6675 K-Type Thermocouple
components.description: K-type thermocouple amplifier with cold-junction compensation, SPI.
components.notes: No breadboard electrical model: the harness serves the MAX6675 SPI word (12-bit temperature at 0.25 degC resolution, thermocouple-input bit) on MISO, framed by CS. CS is resolved from pin_map; DIN/SCK use the AVR SPI peripheral. Temperature comes from the temperature param.

components.name: Pressure Transducer (4-20 mA)
components.description: Industrial two-wire 4-20 mA pressure transmitter.
components.notes: Ideal 4-20 mA loop: I = 4 mA + 16 mA * (pressure - range_min)/(range_max - range_min). A receiver/sense resistor is still needed to read it.

components.name: ACS712 Current Sensor
components.description: Hall-effect AC/DC current sensor module (5A / 20A / 30A variants).
components.notes: Ideal linear output Vout = Vcc/2 + sensitivity * current; the current is a stimulus you set. Supply range, offset drift and bandwidth are not simulated.

components.name: Voltage Sensor Module
components.description: Resistive-divider voltage sensor module (up to ~25 V input).
components.notes: Resistive divider (default 30k/7.5k = 5:1): SIG is a scaled copy of VIN. Connect VIN to the voltage being measured.

components.name: Flame Sensor Module

components.notes: The digital output (OUT/DO) is an ideal push-pull logic level set by the 'detected' stimulus. Supply, thresholds/timing and any analog output (AO) are not simulated.

components.name: Sound / Microphone Sensor Module
